title: Morphisms in $D^b_c(X,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell)$ descend to a finite extension
statement:
Let $X$ be a standing scheme, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite and $C,D\in\Dbc(X,E)$. For finite
$F\supseteq E$ and every $r\in\mathbf Z$:

1. $\Hom_{D(X,F)}(C_F,D_F[r])\cong\Hom_{D(X,E)}(C,\operatorname{Res}D_F[r])$, and likewise over $\Qlb$,
   naturally in $F$;
2. if $D^\bullet$ is a bounded complex representing $D$, then $(D^\bullet\otimes_{E_X}F_X)_F$ is a
   filtered system of complexes of $E_X$-modules vanishing below the lower bound of $D^\bullet$,
   with colimit $D^\bullet\otimes_{E_X}\QbarX$;
3. the map $\varinjlim_F\Hom(C_F,D_F[r])\to\Hom(C_{\Qlb},D_{\Qlb}[r])$ is bijective.

proof.text:
(1) Work in the small pro-étale site in a universe containing its skeleton and the set of finite subextensions. Put $R=E_X$, and let $B$ be either $F_X$ or $\QbarX$. The closed symmetric sheaf tensor of [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor] is additive and preserves colimits. The ordinary extension/restriction adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] therefore applies; restriction is exact, and extension is right exact. The finite-limit preservation in [lem-sfb-subfield-flat] and [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat], respectively, makes extension exact as well. Thus both termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Apply the localization defining the derived category in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] to their unit and counit: naturality holds for images of complex maps and also for inverses of quasi-isomorphisms, and the two triangle identities remain identities after localization. This gives an adjunction on the derived categories without any K-flat-resolution hypothesis. Its bijection is
$$\alpha_B(f)=\operatorname{Res}(f)\circ\eta_C^B,\qquad \eta_C^B:C\longrightarrow\operatorname{Res}(B\otimes_R C),\quad c\longmapsto1\otimes c.$$
The inverse is $g\longmapsto\epsilon\circ(B\otimes_R g)$, with $\epsilon(b\otimes n)=bn$. These formulas and the triangle identities prove clause (1); termwise restriction commutes with every shift.

Here is how the functors of the statement are these termwise ones. In the statement $C_F=T_{E,F}C$ and $C_{\Qlb}=T_{E,\Qlb}C$ are the derived extensions of scalars of [def-sfb-derived-extend-subfield] and [def-sfb-derived-extend-to-qlbar], and $\operatorname{Res}$ is termwise restriction. Both module-level extensions were just shown exact, so the exact-functor clause of [sk-def-sfb-derived-categories] gives natural isomorphisms $T_{E,F}\cong D(F_X\otimes_{E_X}-)$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}\cong D(\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}-)$ with the termwise functors, and likewise $T_{F,F'}$ and $T_{F,\Qlb}$ for the intermediate stages. Transporting the adjunction above along these isomorphisms gives clause (1) for $T_{E,F}$ and $T_{E,\Qlb}$; all computations below are made with the termwise functors. The extension map to $\Qlb$ in clause (3) sends $f\colon C_F\to D_F[r]$ to $\theta_{D[r]}\circ T_{F,\Qlb}(f)\circ\theta_C^{-1}$, where $\theta\colon T_{F,\Qlb}T_{E,F}\cong T_{E,\Qlb}$ is the comparison of [def-sfb-derived-extend-comp-iso]; that definition takes $\theta$ termwise from the isomorphism $\operatorname{Ext}_{F_X\to\QbarX}\operatorname{Ext}_{E_X\to F_X}\cong\operatorname{Ext}_{E_X\to\QbarX}$ carrying the composite unit to the unit. The transitivity isomorphism displayed below, for $B=F_X$ and $B'=\QbarX$, sends $1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to $1\otimes m$, so it carries the composite unit $m\mapsto1\otimes(1\otimes m)$ to the unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$. By the uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-conjugate-iso-unit-equation] (the case of one right adjoint and $\delta=\mathrm{id}$) it is that isomorphism. Hence the map $f\mapsto f_{B'}$ used below is exactly the extension map of clause (3).

Here is the transition calculation. For $B\to B'$ arising from $F\subseteq F'$ or $F\subseteq\Qlb$, the transitivity isomorphism is
$$B'\otimes_B(B\otimes_R M)\longrightarrow B'\otimes_R M,\quad b'\otimes(b\otimes m)\longmapsto b'i(b)\otimes m,$$
with inverse $b'\otimes m\longmapsto b'\otimes(1\otimes m)$. Both maps are balanced and inverse on the displayed generators, hence on the sheaf tensors and termwise on complexes. The coefficient transition $t_M:B\otimes_R M\to B'\otimes_R M$ sends $b\otimes m$ to $i(b)\otimes m$. Thus $t_C\eta_C^B=\eta_C^{B'}$. Naturality of the $B\to B'$ extension unit, first on complexes and then on their localization, gives $\operatorname{Res}(f_{B'})t_C=t_{D[r]}\operatorname{Res}(f)$. Consequently
$$\alpha_{B'}(f_{B'})=t_{D[r]}\alpha_B(f).$$
This proves compatibility with all finite transition maps and with the maps to $\Qlb$.

(2) Let $I$ be the poset of finite subextensions $F\subseteq\Qlb$ containing $E$. It is a set, contains $E$, and is directed by finite composita [det-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed-subextensions]. Restricting the coefficient colimit of [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] to $I$ does not change it: a cocone on $I$ extends to every finite subfield $H$ by $H_X\to(EH)_X$ followed by its cocone leg. For $H\subseteq H'$ the required compatibility follows in $(EH')_X$; if $H$ contains $E$, the extension is the original cocone. These two operations are inverse.

We use this colimit as one of $R$-modules, not just as rings. The module objects identify with ordinary module sheaves: by the sheafified sectionwise tensor in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], an internal action is exactly a compatible sectionwise bilinear action. By [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], module colimits are sheafified sectionwise colimits. For this filtered diagram of $R$-algebras, the sectionwise module colimit has ring multiplication: move two representatives to a common finite stage and multiply there; independence and the ring laws follow at a common stage. Sheafification extends these operations and their equations, so this module colimit is also the ring colimit (a compatible ring cocone induces the module map, which preserves multiplication by its displayed formula). Its vertex is therefore $\QbarX$ with its specified $R$-action.

For a fixed $R$-module $M$, the relative tensor of [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor] is a coequalizer built from the ambient sheaf tensor. That tensor preserves colimits by [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Taking the colimit of these coequalizers is the coequalizer of the colimits: maps out of either object are exactly compatible families of maps satisfying the same balancing equation. Hence
$$\varinjlim_{F\in I}(F_X\otimes_R M)\cong(\varinjlim_{F\in I}F_X)\otimes_R M\cong\QbarX\otimes_R M.$$
Apply this degreewise to $M=D^n$. The maps are induced by $b\otimes m\mapsto i(b)\otimes m$, and the differential is $b\otimes m\mapsto b\otimes d(m)$, so the displayed isomorphisms commute with differentials. If $D^n=0$ for $n<a$, each tensor term is zero in those degrees, proving the common lower bound and clause (2).

(3) The standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ finite type over a field $k$. A field is Noetherian since its only ideals are $0$ and $k$, and $\operatorname{Spec}k$ has one point and is quasi-compact. Therefore [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] makes $X$ Noetherian, as required by [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity]. The same continuity statement explicitly includes every $C\in\Dbc(X,E)$, so its hypothesis on the source object holds.

Choose a bounded complex $D^\bullet$ representing $D$. For completeness, bounded cohomology suffices for this choice: take any representative $K$ and integers $a<b$ outside which its cohomology vanishes. First replace its degree-$b$ term by $\ker d^b$ and set all higher terms to zero; the resulting complex maps to $K$ inducing the same cohomology. Then replace degree $a$ by $\operatorname{coker}d^{a-1}$ and set lower terms to zero; the first truncated complex maps to this bounded complex, again inducing the same cohomology. Both maps are quasi-isomorphisms, giving the required representative. The boundedness used here is that of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible].

Put $K_F^\bullet=F_X\otimes_{E_X}D^\bullet$, regarded by restriction as $E_X$-modules. By (2) these form a small filtered diagram with a common lower bound and termwise colimit $\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}D^\bullet$. Exactness in (1) shows these complexes represent $\operatorname{Res}D_F$ and $\operatorname{Res}D_{\Qlb}$. Apply [sk-lem-constructible-ext-continuity] with $\Lambda=\underline E$ and $q=r$ to obtain
$$\varinjlim_F\Hom_{D(X,E)}(C,K_F^\bullet[r])\xrightarrow{\sim}\Hom_{D(X,E)}(C,(\QbarX\otimes_{E_X}D^\bullet)[r]).$$
The transition identity $\alpha_{B'}(f_{B'})=t_{D[r]}\alpha_B(f)$ proved in (1) identifies its source diagram with the diagram of $\Hom_{D(X,F)}(C_F,D_F[r])$. Taking $B'=\QbarX$ in that same identity identifies every cocone leg with extension of scalars to $\Qlb$. Thus this bijection is precisely the map of clause (3), for every integer $r$.

Exactness comes from lem-sfb-subfield-flat and lem-sfb-qlbar-flat. Step 3: the Noetherian hypothesis comes from finite type over a field via lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian; continuity covers every bounded constructible C for Λ=E; the τ≤b, τ≥a bounded representative is correct; q=r.
